physical.title: Two native spherical thick lenses, finite mirror, and an explicit finite aperture

interpretation.requestedResult: Simulate actual pinned-native rays through two finite thick lenses, an independent finite mirror, and a separately positioned finite aperture. Observe native absorption and sampled crossings without prescribing a ray itinerary.
assumptions: This apparatus is synthetic and physically explicit, not a textbook problem interpretation.
Exactly two separate nonrotated biconvex finite spherical thick lenses share explicit exterior refractive index 1.
The mirror is finite and may be missed; no return itinerary is encoded.
Native-deep-v17 permits at most 16 native ray interactions, without changing the older versions' maximum 8.
Fresnel-off is an explicit approximation that neglects partial reflection but keeps total internal reflection.
The v18 finite aperture is a centered transparent 20 mm opening with two native opaque arms; it is vertical and at least 0.01 mm outside both lens x envelopes and other finite surface planes.
Native-deep-v18 is an explicit version-scoped maximum of 16 native interactions; v1–v16 remain at depth 8 and v17 retains native-deep-v17.
unknowns: Native sampled interactions alone do not establish a complete image, beam power, source-to-detector ancestry or full Fresnel tree.
One native crossing or absorbed sample does not establish a continuous shadow, PSF, optical image, flux, or source-specific detector attribution.
